content: The National Health Federation (NHF) is an international non-profit organization dedicated to consumer education and health freedom. It advocates for individuals' rights to choose healthy foods, take dietary supplements, and utilize alternative therapies without government interference. The NHF is unique in being the only consumer health freedom organization globally with official observer status at Codex Alimentarius Commission meetings, the highest international body on food standards. This status allows the NHF to speak out for health freedom at these meetings. The NHF was founded in 1955 by Fred Hart, making it the world’s oldest health freedom organization. Hart’s motivation stemmed from his frustration with orthodox medicine, which denied his wife, Eva, an alternative treatment for her breast cancer. He was also angered by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s restrictions on health food stores sharing information about their products. Over the decades, the NHF has been involved in numerous campaigns, including mandatory poultry inspection in the 1950s, legal licensing for chiropractors in the 1960s, opposition to fluoridation in the 1970s, and legislative recognition of acupuncture in the 1980s. In the 1990s, the NHF played a significant role in the passage of the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act (DSHEA) and continued to fight against malathion spraying, promote public education on vaccine risks, and oppose fluoridation. In recent years, the NHF has expanded its activities internationally, becoming a prominent organization in opposing Codex Alimentarius Commission efforts to restrict consumer access to vitamins, minerals, and natural health information. Despite its global focus, the NHF continues to challenge U.S. legislation that threatens access to healthy foods, dietary supplements, and alternative therapies. The NHF’s leadership includes Scott Tips, its President and Treasurer, who is a California-licensed attorney specializing in food and drug law, trademark law, and nonprofit organizations. Tips has served as the NHF’s General Counsel since 1989 and writes a monthly column for Whole Foods Magazine. The Vice President, Dr. James Privitera, is a physician with a background in internal medicine, allergy, immunology, and nutrition. The Chairman, Paul Anthony Taylor, has a background in the music industry and is well-versed in Codex Alimentarius operations, having attended numerous meetings and authored articles on health freedom. The Vice-Chairman, Dr. Murray Susser, is a physician with a history in the U.S. Air Force and expertise in integrative medicine. The Secretary, Sylvia Kresevich Provenza, is an active member in recruiting for the organization and leads the Pittsburgh-Western Pennsylvania Chapter. The NHF has local chapters, such as the Pittsburgh-Western Pennsylvania Chapter and the Southern Maine Chapter, which have been active since the late 1950s. The organization also hosts health expos and conventions across the United States, ranging from small booths to large three-day events with numerous speakers and thousands of attendees, catering to the alternative healthcare community. The NHF’s stated aims include the following rights and freedoms for individuals: 1. The right to control one’s own body, including decisions about food, drink, and medicines. 2. The right to supplement diets with vitamins, minerals, herbs, amino acids, and enzymes without government restrictions. 3. The right to receive alternative medical treatments without government interference. 4. The right of alternative medical practitioners to determine and use treatments best suited for their patients. 5. The right of manufacturers and distributors to provide truthful research and labeling information about dietary supplements. 6. The right to discuss and disseminate truthful natural health information without government suppression. 7. Freedom from restrictive international Codex Alimentarius standards that threaten health freedoms. 8. The right to consume clean, fresh food free of pesticides, hormones, antibiotics, poisons, or irradiation. 9. The right to breathe clean air and drink water free of harmful chemicals like fluoride. 10. The right to protect oneself and one’s children from unnecessary and potentially dangerous childhood vaccines. 11. The right of military personnel to refuse mandatory vaccines, such as anthrax. 12. The right to keep medical records private and confidential. The NHF publishes a quarterly magazine, Health Freedom News, edited by Scott Tips. The magazine covers topics such as nutrition, alternative healthcare, and health freedom, providing valuable information to its readers.
